subject: Latency envelope clarification and PoC test plan for Veridian
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: clarifying latency envelope and PoC scoping

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a focused PoC for latency qualification (p95/p99 end-to-end):

Summary of what we heard:
- Your app: multi-turn assistant in a web client + mobile app; model calls originate from your backend service (not directly from browsers).
- Current provider: CloudPrompt; you observe occasional p99 spikes during peak traffic.
- Primary goals for PoC: validate end-to-end p95/p99 under production-like concurrency and confirm streaming behavior for partial results.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm numbers where possible?):
1) Measurement point: Where do you measure your current p95/p99? (browser RUM, backend ingress timestamp, or upstream client?) We need to align on timestamp semantics for end-to-end.
2) Target envelope: you mentioned wanting best-effort p95 ~300-400ms and p99 <800ms — can you confirm firm targets vs aspirational?
3) Concurrency profile: typical sustained concurrency (RPS or concurrent requests) and peak burst (short-term concurrency).
4) Payloads: average input length (tokens / characters), and typical output length. Any large outliers we should account for?
5) Streaming: you indicated streaming is required for incremental UI updates. Is client-side partial-delivery required for all flows or only for the assistant?
6) Cache/warmup: do you expect warm KV cache (hot model state) at PoC start, or should we simulate cold-start behavior?

Proposed next steps we can run in-parallel once you confirm:
- We’ll prepare a short synthetic harness that measures p95/p99 from Redwood’s test agent (server-side) and a browser-style RUM harness if you can provide a token.
- You share a sample APM trace and a representative traffic capture (redacted), we’ll map timestamps.
- Align on a 2-hour sustained run + a 15-minute stress window.

I attached a simple PoC scoping sheet for you to fill (PoC_scoping_sheet.xlsx) — please return with numbers and any existing SLI definitions.

If easier, we can run a 30-minute sync tomorrow to finalize. Proposed windows: Tue 05/04 10–11am PT or Wed 05/05 2–3pm PT.

Thanks — looking forward to narrowing this down.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: PoC_scoping_sheet.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Elena Rossi <elena@veridian.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:08:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: clarifying latency envelope and PoC scoping

Tessa — great summary, thanks. Answers inline below.

1) Measurement point: we primarily look at backend ingress -> last-byte at backend (so server-side end-to-end). We do have RUM, but we want server-side verification first.
2) Target envelope: our product/ops team has set target p95 = 350ms, p99 = 720ms for the assistant flows. Those are enforceable delivery targets for our SLA.
3) Concurrency profile: typical sustained concurrency is ~40 concurrent inferences (roughly 20 RPS given our request sizes). Peak bursts during event spikes hit ~140–160 concurrent for short windows (1–5 minutes).
4) Payloads: average request ~80 tokens in, ~160 tokens out. We have some long-context flows (~800 tokens out) but they are ~0.5% of traffic.
5) Streaming: streaming partials are required for the assistant UX; mobile clients show improved engagement with partial tokens. We need streaming enabled end-to-end.
6) Cache/warmup: production has warm caches; for PoC please assume warm cache, but we’d like one cold-start scenario too.

Attaching a small APM extract and a representative trace that shows the spikes (veridian_apm_trace_20270428.json).

We can do the scheduling you proposed — Tue 05/04 10–11am PT works for our engineering lead. Please share Redwood test credentials and the endpoints you’ll use for the harness.

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Engineering
Veridian AI
attachments: veridian_apm_trace_20270428.json (json)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@veridian.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 13:02:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: clarifying latency envelope and PoC scoping

Elena — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. A few technical clarifications from the Redwood side so our measurements line up with yours: 

- Timestamp alignment: our harness will emit both client-side (test agent) timestamps and server-side ingress/egress markers. To match your backend ingress->last-byte definition, can you confirm a single canonical timestamp field in your logs (e.g., "request_received_ts")? If not, we’ll work from the APM trace you sent to map fields.
- Warm cache: acknowledged — we’ll run the primary verification with warm models. For the cold-start scenario we’ll schedule an isolated run and capture the first N requests.
- Streaming semantics: we support chunked streaming and will exercise both streaming and non-streaming endpoints. For streaming, we need to confirm whether you require SSE or HTTP/2 chunking.
- Measurement harness: propose the following PoC phases:
  Phase A — Instrumentation & alignment (1 day): exchange logs/APM, confirm timestamp mapping and SLI definitions.
  Phase B — Synthetic server-side verification (2 hour sustained run + 15 minute stress burst): measures p95/p99 with representative payloads and concurrency profile you provided.
  Phase C — Client-side / RUM verification (optional): run a browser-style harness to capture perceived latency.

Can you also confirm whether your incumbent (CloudPrompt) uses any request-level preprocessing that would change tokenization or effective model input size? Small differences here can change latency profiles.

We’ll provision a Redwood PoC test account and a pair of endpoints (streaming + non-streaming). Tessa — I’ll need the final filled scoping sheet to make the test workload.

Available windows for the Phase B run: Tue 05/04 10:00–12:30 PT (we can do the 2-hour sustained + stress burst inside that window) or Thu 05/06 08:00–11:00 PT. If Tue works, we’ll send credentials this evening.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: clarifying latency envelope and PoC scoping

Marcus / Tessa — Tue 05/04 10:00–12:30 PT is confirmed. Our engineering lead (same call) will run the CloudPrompt baseline trace at the start of the window so we can compare side-by-side.

Action items before Tue: 
- Redwood: share test credentials and the streaming + non-streaming endpoints (please include TLS and auth instructions).
- Veridian: we’ll return the completed PoC_scoping_sheet.xlsx and a sanitized sample of request logs (request_received_ts included).

One more note — we will expect the PoC report to include p95/p99 computed over the server-side ingress->last-byte metric, plus a short appendix describing any differences between Redwood-measured and CloudPrompt baseline numbers.

See you Tue — Elena

Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Engineering
Veridian AI
